notes: Screening policy has moved: the NHS PSA page (as retrieved) says no national programme, while the UK NSC final recommendation (March 2026 meeting, published May 2026) recommends targeted PSA screening every 2 years for men aged 45 to 61 with a pathogenic BRCA2 variant and a family history of breast, ovarian, pancreatic or prostate cancer, and gov.uk says ministers in England agreed to implement; no start date retrieved. Final text states both without claiming the programme is running. The PHE 2016 'man aged 50+ can ask GP' statement comes from one search summary of an old blog and is flagged for human review. Macmillan (under 65) and Prostate Cancer UK (under 60) disagree on family-history age so no age is stated. No urgent route (999/NHS 111) was found for prostate cancer symptoms on the NHS page, so only the NHS non-urgent GP advice is stated. ProtecT, recurrence, DRE finding gloss, 'clearest BRCA2 link', pancreatic relatives, surgery side effects removed as unretrieved. Search summaries blend pages, so some URL attributions are to the page titled in results. Reference to 'NCI' and 'MedlinePlus' dropped as not re-retrieved.
